_note: Seed-assignment record (historical): which member ran which arm on which seeds. ONE member trained directly on the final map (Lv3); the other FOUR trained level by level (Lv1 -> Lv2 -> Lv3). Arms were fixed per member and only the seeds varied, run in the order listed; the first seed of each block was required. analyze.py reads this file for its seed-status table and adapts to whatever seeds are present; tests/test_smoke.py checks the split and the seed allocation stay valid.
design: unpaired, 4 curriculum runs per round vs 1 direct run per round
why_multiple_seeds: With one round each the arms are 4-vs-1: the control arm's run-to-run spread is unmeasurable and the run-level permutation test has only C(5,1)=5 label assignments, so its smallest possible p is 0.2 — the design cannot reach p<0.05 no matter what the data say. A SECOND round each makes it 8-vs-2 and the floor drops to 1/C(10,8) = 0.022. That one extra round is the highest-value compute in the whole experiment, and the single highest-value run in it is the direct member's second: until it exists, nothing can estimate how much of the control arm's score is seed luck.
seed_allocation: Base seeds 1..5 go to member1..member5 in order. Each extra round adds +10 to the member's base seed, so member i owns the block {i, i+10, i+20, ...} and no two members can ever collide. Seed 0 is deliberately unassigned: it is train.py's default, so a results file named *_seed0.json means somebody dropped their --seed, and analyze.py will flag it as unclaimed rather than silently folding it into an arm.

arms.direct: configs/lv3_direct.json (from scratch on the final map, same total env steps)

matched_pairs_are_optional_here: Because every member owns a private seed block, no seed appears in both arms, so the planned runs produce no matched pairs and analyze.py's paired test stays off. That costs almost nothing: the paired sign-flip test's floor is 2/2^k (0.5 at two pairs, 0.25 at three), i.e. far weaker than the unpaired test it would sit next to. If wanted, one spare run of the OTHER arm on a seed the first arm already used creates a pair, and the paired test switches itself on at two.
if_you_run_out_of_listed_seeds: Further runs continue with +10 in a member's block (35, 45, ...). Any seed not in this file is accepted by the scripts as a spare run; they only refuse to overwrite an existing result file (FORCE=1 overrides that).
